rationale: Measuring the one consequence the asserted defect had not yet witnessed: what each trigger actually does once the node's store sits below its snapshot index. The harness drives a real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0 and a high SnapshotThreshold to the emptied state, records store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot, then calls the production takeSnapshot twice and records the same operands after each call. Native construction feedback with these fixed inputs gave: emptied state store_last=0, snapshot_index=3, applied=3, stored snapshots=1, should_snapshot=true; then two successful takeSnapshot calls that each created another snapshot at the unchanged index 3 while applied stayed 3, taking the stored count to 3. That is the redundant work the claim predicts, repeatable rather than a one-off. The same run also exposed a store-specific detail worth recording: after the second compaction the InmemStore reported store_last=18446744073709551615, so the trigger fired there through a wrapped store index rather than a delta subtraction; the generic emptied-store reading is the first sample, and I am noting the artifact so it is not folded into the claim. This submission records the fixed experiment for controller execution; the measured interpretation is left for the retained receipt.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold=10000 and SnapshotInterval=1h. After the node becomes leader one command is applied and a user Snapshot() is run, then store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded. The production takeSnapshot is then invoked twice, and after each invocation the same operands are recorded together with the returned snapshot-id presence and any error.

experiment.prefix: inmemConfig supplies the defaults; TrailingLogs=0 makes the compaction triggered by the user snapshot trim up to the snapshot index and the large threshold makes the control verdict false before that. MakeCluster(1, t, conf) starts the real node over InmemTransport with InmemStore for logs and stable state; the test waits for Leader before applying so the apply is accepted. takeSnapshot is the package-internal production routine that runSnapshots calls on its own timer, so invoking it directly removes the wait on SnapshotInterval while still exercising the production snapshot, compaction and configuration-read paths and the FSM's Snapshot call; no production logic is modified and all operands are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List().
